lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: entry requirements and realistic timelines

objective: For two pathways the learner is seriously considering, learners research and record the actual entry requirements (such as GPA, test scores, application steps, required hours, or qualification standards) and build a realistic timeline, practicing the discipline of verifying requirements from a real source rather than guessing or assuming.
scenario: The learner picks two pathways from their day-1 'worth investigating further' list, looks up the actual entry requirements for each from a named, checkable source, and lays out a realistic month-by-month or year-by-year timeline for meeting those requirements before graduation.
safetyNotes: Research for this lesson uses publicly available program or organization information; no account is created and no personal or household information is submitted anywhere.
materials: access to look up program or organization information

tasks.directions: Before researching, write down what you currently assume the entry requirements are for your two chosen pathways.

prompts.text: Name your two chosen pathways, and for each one write your best guess at what it takes to get in or get started, before you check anything.

tasks.directions: Look up the actual entry requirements for each pathway from a specific, named source, and record them.

prompts.text: For pathway one, list the actual entry requirements you found (such as GPA, test scores, application steps, required hours, or qualification standards) and name the specific source you used.
For pathway two, list the actual entry requirements you found and name the specific source you used.
For both pathways, I named a specific, checkable source rather than relying on memory or a guess.

tasks.directions: Build a realistic timeline for meeting the requirements of each pathway before you'd need them.

prompts.text: For each pathway, lay out a realistic timeline of the steps you would need to complete and roughly when, working backward from when the requirement would be due.

tasks.directions: Compare your warm-up guesses to what you actually found.

prompts.text: Which of your warm-up guesses turned out to be wrong or incomplete once you checked a real source, and what was the gap?

remediation: If the recorded requirements are vague or unsourced (for example, 'good grades' with no source named), reteach by modeling how to find one specific, verifiable requirement from a named source together, then have the learner independently find and record one additional specific requirement for each pathway using that same method.
extension: Have the learner identify one requirement on either timeline that depends on something outside their direct control (such as a required exam offered only on certain dates, or a minimum age), and write a backup plan for what they would do if that requirement were missed or delayed.
